messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate from Stripe API for webhook deliveries (>15% 5m). Alerting oncall. https://status.stripe.com/ (automated)

alex (eng-oncall): seeing 429 spikes and 502s from stripe in the delivery worker logs. failures started ~9:30 UTC. paging maya now.

pagerduty: Paging maya (SRE) — escalation triggered for incidents channel.

maya (sre): on it. can someone paste the datadog query/dashboard? I want to confirm regions/hosts impacted.

alex (eng-oncall): datadog: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/stripe-webhook-delivery (filtered) — ETA: 9:32 UTC spike from eu-west-1 and us-east-1 pods. error samples: 429, 502, 500 from stripe.com/v1/webhooks.

maya (sre): thanks. quick check: is this hitting our webhook workers only or also direct API calls (billing sync, invoices)?

alex (eng-oncall): primarily workers (async webhook fanout). we also see retries from invoice-sync jobs backing up (queue depth +400).

prashant (product): heads up — billing webhook failures cause delayed invoice email generation for some customers. want an early estimate of customer impact please.

sylvia (cs): I already have a couple customers pinging support about delayed invoices. need ETA for a mitigation or a rollback plan.

maya (sre): mitigation plan options: 1) throttle webhook worker concurrency to reduce request rate to Stripe, 2) enable safer retry/backoff (exponential jitter), 3) switch to polling fallback for critical billing webhooks (short term), 4) contact Stripe support for quota/billing enforcement info.

alex (eng-oncall): I can flip the worker concurrency env var for the delivery queue now. current concurrency=50 per region. propose dropping to 10 to reduce sustained RPS.

maya (sre): do it. also add a 1s -> 30s backoff cap on retryers if possible. we should preserve idempotency.

alex (eng-oncall): running command now:
```bash
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/webhook-delivery WORKER_CONCURRENCY=10 --record
```

alex (eng-oncall): done. rolling restart started, pods terminating with new env. monitoring.

maya (sre): lowering concurrency reduced RPS to Stripe by ~70% within 45s. 429 rate dipped but retries still causing small bursts. queue depth still high (~320).

prashant (product): what's the customer impact number? any estimate % of accounts affected or invoices delayed?

sylvia (cs): sampling support queue: ~12 open tickets explicitly about delayed invoices in last 30 mins. that's ~0.3% of active billing customers based on our rough numbers. could be larger for high-volume merchants.

maya (sre): I'm enabling polling fallback for invoice status for customers with high throughput so they don't rely on webhooks for immediate events. This will reduce webhook fanout temporarily.

alex (eng-oncall): toggling feature flag: `billing.polling_fallback = true` for enterprise and critical merchants.

alex (eng-oncall): feature flag applied. triggering faster invoice-sync job for flagged mercheants.

maya (sre): also opened a support ticket with Stripe (ref 13124) asking if they have quota enforcement/billing-side throttles in place; sharing their initial status page note about degraded webhook delivery.

prashant (product): good. please prepare customer-safe messaging: short note explaining delayed invoices due to upstream Stripe rate limiting, ETA for resolution (we should say monitoring + mitigation in progress). sylvia to draft.

sylvia (cs): drafting now: "We're seeing delayed invoice delivery for some customers due to upstream payment provider rate limits. We're reducing traffic and pausing webhook fanout for affected accounts to restore queues. We'll follow up once deliveries resume." will post to support channels in 15m.

maya (sre): monitoring logs: sample delivery error payload:
```json
{"error": {"type":"rate_limit_error","message":"Too many requests to Stripe API"}}
```

maya (sre): after concurrency change and polling fallback, error rate down to ~3% 5m. queue draining rate improved to ~+120 jobs/min. good trend.

alex (eng-oncall): starting controlled canary to reintroduce higher concurrency for low-volume accounts in 10m to see if Stripe has lifted limits. will monitor real-time.

pagerduty: Note: handoff scheduled in 30m to next oncall.

maya (sre): handing off to alex in 30m. alex will maintain mitigation knobs and keep CS updated. I'll stay on standby for escalation.

alex (eng-oncall): acknowledged. tracking actions: 1) keep concurrency=10 until error rate <1% stable for 15m, 2) keep polling fallback on for flagged customers, 3) keep Stripe ticket open and paste updates, 4) CS msg posted, 5) follow-up postmortem if root cause is Stripe billing/quota enforcement.

prashant (product): once we confirm full recovery, let's prepare an internal blameless postmortem and runbook update: add automatic polling fallback for known billing webhooks and a preconfigured circuit-breaker when provider 429s exceed threshold.

sylvia (cs): support note posted. customers responded, some appreciative of temporary fixes. will collate affected accounts list and escalate high-touch customers to success managers.

maya (sre): final status at 9:54 UTC: system stable, error rate 0.6% 5m, queues draining. keeping incident open for monitoring and Stripe follow-up.

alex (eng-oncall): closing pager for now but keeping thread open until Stripe confirms no quota enforcement change on their side.

incident-bot: Incident unresolved — monitoring. update required in 60m or on status change.
